items.title: Hinton Milt — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I knew his mother, Kate Johnson... She said, 'His name is Albert Johnson and he plays with the Earl Hines band'.

ctx.x: Bus, yes. Had a terrible accident and one of the great tenor players, Cecil Irvin was his name, he was killed and Billy Franklin, the trombone was just maimed up terribly. Several guys were hurt and it was just… wrecked the band pretty badly. A lot of young guys came in. Bud Johnson was one of the young guys. He came in and he was beginning to write… and doing some writing and getting the feel of things. One of the stories that he tells, which is quite true because I knew his mother, Kate Johnson… his mother…

“Well I‟ve got a son that plays in Chicago. The guy said, “Well I‟m going to Chicago, what‟s his name”? She said, “His name is Albert Johnson and he plays with the Earl Hines band”. So this man said, “Well I‟ve got a band and I‟m going to Chicago, I‟ll check him out”. So one night while Bud was playing with Earl Hines, the waiter says, “There‟s a gentleman over at the table that wants to talk to you. Bud goes over the table and the guy says, “I met your mother in Dallas, she told me you were here. The band sounds…
